extracted.intended_audience: students and scholars of algebra/historical mathematics (readers of Italian Renaissance mathematical treatises)
extracted.subtask_description: Rules, definitions and procedural methods for manipulating binomials, their 'reciprocals'/'residues', medials, and related line/area constructions as presented in a historical Italian algebra/geometric treatise. Includes methods to form binomials with prescribed residues and to operate on lines and areas to produce desired proportionalities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of a binomio (binomial) and its components
rubrics_metrics.description: A binomio is described as composed of its root (radice) and its remainder/term of subtraction (termine del meno) — i.e., the two component lines or quantities that form the binomial.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The text repeatedly states that a binomio 'si forma con lo termino del meno' and that the binomio 'risponde suo recifo e composto del meno', clarifying that to understand or construct binomials one must identify the principal term and its complementary term (major/minor). Examples and symbolic exemplars (e.g., notations like 2o, m, 4o) illustrate components.

rubrics_metrics.name: Concept of recifo/reciduo (reciprocal/residue) of a binomial
rubrics_metrics.description: The work defines several 'recifi' (first, second, third, fourth, fifth, etc.) associated with a binomio — residues or reciprocal-like constructions related to the binomial's components.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each recifo is tied to operations on components (e.g., 'primo recifo', 'secondo recifo', 'terzo recifo' etc.). The text explains how to order and obtain these recifi and gives numeric symbolic examples for each. It also links recifi to powers (quadrati, quarti) and to geometric constructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule for producing reciprocals by multiplying components in like fashion
rubrics_metrics.description: To obtain corresponding recifi for different binomials, multiply each binomial's components in the same manner — i.e., operate uniformly across binomials so their recifi correspond.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The text prescribes multiplying 'ciascuno in se medesimo' (each by itself) and performing the same operations on corresponding binomials so that the first recifo of one corresponds to the first of another, etc. Examples show applying identical exponents/powers to component lines to preserve correspondence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of powers (quadrati, quarti) and taking fractional parts to form residues
rubrics_metrics.description: Residues and roots are often constructed by taking squares, fourth parts or parts of powers: e.g., 'quarta parte la … radici', 'la quinta parte', and using these parts in construction of recifi.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The text shows operations such as forming the fourth part of a square or the square of sums to obtain terms of the binomial or its recifo. It provides algebraic-symbolic examples and procedural commentary on selecting which power/part to take depending on desired recifo.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition and role of the linea adiecta (adjoined line) in residues
rubrics_metrics.description: An 'adjoined line' commensurable or incommensurable with others is used to express residues: the residue between lines in powers and commensurabilities is represented by an adjoined line.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The text explains that the adjoined line (linea adiecta) when rational and commensurable in length with others is the named residue (e.g., 'refiduo quarta'). It shows how adding or appending such a line affects power relations and residues of binomials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bi-medial line and its consequence on irrational residues
rubrics_metrics.description: The 'linea bimediale' (bi-medial) arises when a line related to medials produces irrational quantities or residues; such lines produce incommensurable numbers relative to ordinary lengths.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The treatise notes that a bi-medial line produces irrational numbers when combined with other medials; it gives examples where multiplication involving a bi-medial yields irrational residues and links to Euclidean propositions about medials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ordering of recifi (first through fifth etc.) and their correspondence
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipi are ordered (primo, secondo, terzo, quarto, quinto) and there is an explicit correspondence: the first recifo corresponds to the first binomial component, the second to the second, etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The text enumerates the recifi and states that 'quelli per ordine sono primo secondo terzo quarto quinto sesto', indicating procedures to compute each and how they relate to binomial components and to each other in multiplicative and additive operations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure to find a binomial given a desired recifo
rubrics_metrics.description: One finds a binomial having a given recifo by imposing the conditions that define which recifo is sought (e.g., by prescribing the term used to 'dirimpio' or the power whose part will serve as the residue) and constructing component lines accordingly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The author gives stepwise guidance: choose which recifo is desired, select the appropriate power/part (e.g., fourth part), and form the binomial by combining the chosen principal term and the term that will produce the given recifo when used in the prescribed operation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule linking commensurability of lines to rational or irrational residues
rubrics_metrics.description: If component lines are rational and commensurable in certain ways then residues (recifi) are rational; if lines are incommensurable the residues are irrational; proportional relations determine whether residues are rational multiples.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The text repeatedly distinguishes cases: commensurable in length vs incommensurable, and notes consequences for residues and constructed binomials (e.g., 'se fuesse rationali… il refiduo… verametega un altro modo'). Euclidean reasoning about commensurability is invoked.

rubrics_metrics.name: Method of multiplication to transform sums of squares into areas/products
rubrics_metrics.description: Multiplying certain lines (sides) and taking sums of squares or products is used to obtain areas that correspond to the constructed residues or to 'square' one figure by another (e.g., 'il qdrato de la summa de la multiplicazione…')
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The text explains when to multiply lines and how the product or sum of squares relates geometrically to the desired area — giving examples of multiplying a side by itself, or comparing square of one to square of another to deduce relations used in constructing binomials and recifi.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of repeated demonstration: employing multiple ways to exhibit same truth
rubrics_metrics.description: The author recommends demonstrating propositions by multiple methods: simpler/vulgar demonstrations for intuition and more rigorous demonstrations for correctness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Passages stress that some demonstrations are given 'vulgarmete' for ease, while others are more formal; the treatise suggests both arithmetic and geometric demonstrations to make results evident and to aid comprehension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notation and naming conventions for major/minor and powers
rubrics_metrics.description: The text establishes naming conventions: 'magio' (major), 'mino' (minor), names for moon/other, and conventions for representing powers and their numeric symbolic notation (e.g., .4o, .m, 2o etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These conventions are used to refer compactly to terms and their powers across examples; the treatise uses them to show how to form recifi and to name lines produced by operations (e.g., 'il magio nome de luna…').

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule: corresponding operations must be applied to corresponding binomials
rubrics_metrics.description: When constructing corresponding recifi for different binomials, apply the same operations (multiplications/exponentiations) to each binomial's corresponding parts so the produced recifi are in correspondence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The author illustrates with examples: multiply the first part of each binomial by itself if that is done in the first example, and do the same in the second to retain correspondence. This underlies methods for building families of binomials with analogous residues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Construction of quadrinomio and decomposition in multiplicative processes
rubrics_metrics.description: Multiplication of binomials can produce a quadrinomial (four-term expression), whose decomposition and analysis yield residues and relations needed for recifi and other constructions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The text references 'quarto binomio' and 'quadrinomio' and explains how, in multiplying binomials, terms combine to form multi-term expressions whose parts correspond to particular power terms or residues; guidance includes how to isolate and use these parts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Principle of proportionality for areas produced by multiplied lines
rubrics_metrics.description: Areas obtained by multiplying lines (rectangles) follow proportionality rules: multiplying different pairs yields areas proportional according to the component lines, and such proportionality is used to compare and deduce residues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The treatise uses Euclidean proportional reasoning: if lines are multiplied in different ways, the resulting areas sum or subtract to produce target areas; examples show combining rectangles to obtain sums equal to other constructed areas.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guidance on choosing which 'via' (method) to apply among alternatives
rubrics_metrics.description: When multiple methods can demonstrate or produce the same construction, choose according to clarity and the required rigor — give the simpler demonstration for intuition and the longer one for formal proof.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Author remarks that many propositions can be shown by 'piu vie' and often gives the more useful approach or the one that makes the rule clearer; selects methods that avoid unnecessary complication when possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rules for naming and operating with fractional/compound proportions
rubrics_metrics.description: When lines or numbers are in compound proportions (e.g., repeated proportional relations like 4, 5, 6 etc.), their squared or multiplied values follow systematic naming and can be decomposed into known combinations (e.g., 9, 25, 56 combinations).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Text gives explicit numeric examples of such compound proportions and explains how to reduce them or recognize equivalences among squared terms to facilitate constructing residues and recognizing commensurabilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Operational rule: preserving nature, quality, and quantity when forming corresponding recifi
rubrics_metrics.description: When one intends a recifo to correspond 'in natura, qualita e quantita' to another, one must replicate the same constitutive conditions (same nature of components, same measurements) across constructions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Author stresses that 'in natura qualita e quantita' must be kept when making corresponding recifi: e.g., if the first recifo is formed by taking the fourth part of a square, to get the corresponding recifo elsewhere one must apply the same fourth-part operation to the corresponding component.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification of which recifi are real/rational roots vs. irrational
rubrics_metrics.description: Some recifi correspond to real rational roots, others to irrational roots depending on whether components are commensurable; the text identifies conditions under which recifi are 'radici reali' or 'irrazionali'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples and Euclidean references clarify that when the constructed recifo results from commensurable rational lines the root is rational (e.g., 'il quinto recifo… reali radice'), while combinations involving medials/bi-medials lead to irrational residues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure for repeated multiplication and reduction to obtain target residues
rubrics_metrics.description: By repeatedly multiplying lines by given factors and reducing (subtracting common terms), one can obtain the specified residues; the treatise details iterative multiplication and simplification steps.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The text contains stepwise numeric-symbolic examples showing multiple multiplications (e.g., repeated .4o, .m, .7) and reductions to isolate the desired recifo or to form binomials having given properties.
